Three persons have been killed and seven others injured in two separate road crashes along the Sagamu-Ikorodu Expressway and the Ota–Idiroko Road in Ogun State. Sunday PUNCH gathered that the accidents occurred on Saturday at the Kam Steel axis of the Sagamu–Ikorodu Expressway and the Agarawu, Winners axis of the Ota–Idiroko Road. The spokesperson for the Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency, Babatunde Akinbiyi, confirmed the incidents in a traffic update on Saturday. Akinbiyi stated that the first accident occurred at the Kam Steel axis of the Sagamu–Ikorodu Highway, leaving a woman dead and two other women with injuries. He noted that the crash, which occurred at about 4:10 p.m., reportedly happened when a patrol van emerged from the Kam Steel access road onto the highway and collided with a tricycle, causing it to somersault. The TRACE spokesperson said two persons—a man and a woman—died while five others sustained injuries in another accident at the Agarawu, Winners axis of the Ota–Idiroko Road. He added that the crash was caused by brake failure, which reportedly made the truck driver lose control. “According to the eyewitness account, the brake of the Howo truck failed, and the driver lost control and collided with the tricycle. “Nine people were involved; two persons, including a male adult and a female adult, died while seven others were injured,” he stated. Akinbiyi said the injured victims had been taken to the hospital before the arrival of rescue officials. He added that one of the deceased was claimed by her relatives, while the other body was deposited at the General Hospital morgue, Ifo. Akinbiyi said the intervention of TRACE operatives and other emergency responders helped to restore traffic flow at both accident scenes. “While TRACE, FRSC, and the Police commiserate with families of the deceased, motorists are again admonished to make safety their watchword by servicing and adequately maintaining their vehicles as and when due in view of the attendant consequences of non-compliance,” he concluded.
